pages.text: "Red! Wild raspberries!" Rudi the hungry squirrel picked a red berry from a bush. Without even looking, Rudi popped it into their mouth. Behind them, Mei the timid baby goat called, "Rudi!"
"Today I'll pick the most and make a big pie tonight!" Rudi's apron pocket already bulged. But the berry tasted strange.
"Ugh! Bitter!" Rudi's tongue tingled, and their mouth stung. Rudi spat it out and rinsed with water from the flask. Mei's eyes widened.
Mei pointed at the bush. "These leaves aren't raspberry leaves." Rudi looked closely. They really had no pointed edges. Their tongue still tingled.
That evening, Grandma placed a wild raspberry pie on the long table. Rudi took a bite but couldn't taste anything. "My tongue still tingles..." Rudi's shoulders drooped.
Grandma sat beside Rudi and opened her palms. Wild raspberries on one side, those red berries on the other. "They look very alike, don't they? Even I need to look at them in my hands."
"When you see something like this, pick it and bring it to me," said Grandma. Rudi patted their apron pocket. "Unknown berries? Show Grandma!"

The next day, Rudi saw red berries in the forest again. The hand going to their mouth stopped and slipped them into the pocket instead. Rudi brought their big tail forward and wrapped it around their body.
In front of Mei, Rudi counted on their fingers. "One, don't eat what I don't know! Two, put it in my pocket! Three, show Grandma!" Mei slipped berries into their pocket too.
Today's pie was sweet and tart. Grandma stroked Rudi's big tail across her lap. Wait and ask, and you won't miss the real flavor. "So that's the taste! Unknown berries? Show Grandma!"
